history.period: Renovated 1912 (Shake 1834) by Sadguru Govind Maharaj; idols regarded as swayambhu (self-manifested)
history.summary: Padmalaya is the 'half peeth' of the two-and-a-half Ganapati peeths of India. Its stone sanctum houses two swayambhu Ganesh idols on a single Vyaspeeth, named Aamod and Pramod, both of coral stone, one with its trunk curving right and the other left. Legend says Bhim, after slaying the demon Bakasura, struck his elbow on the ground to quench his thirst, forming the nearby Bhimkund pond. The name blends 'Padma' (lotus) and 'Alaya' (home) from a lotus pond beside the temple; it is also called Prabhakshetra. The padukas of Shree Govind Maharaj and a 440-kg bell stand before the temple. name: Shree Kshetra Padmalaya
town_description: Padmalaya is a village in Erandol taluka of Jalgaon district in North Maharashtra, about 10 km from Erandol and 30 km from the district headquarters Jalgaon. The Anjani river flows about 1 km away. It is a small rural pilgrimage village best known for its hilltop Ganesha temple and the nearby Bhimkund pond.
